html:
SMTO-LLM-0090 — Your model service has tool use turned off

GUID: 49faff52-7447-4e7f-813f-4629fc69940a
Slug: provider-tool-calling-disabled
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • Your model can answer in plain text, but its service refused the kind of request SMTO uses to carry out actions. SMTO can't do tasks with this model until that is switched on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell the person who runs the model service (the program that hosts your AI model) that it rejected SMTO because automatic tool calling is turned off. Only they can change how the model service starts; SMTO can't switch this on from its side.
  2. When they have restarted the model service, open Settings › Setup › Model routing and select Check saved model on the card for that model (Main, Helper or Vision). It sends one small test request and confirms the service now accepts the action requests SMTO needs.
  3. Before asking SMTO to continue a task that stopped with this error, open its Conversation and check which steps it already finished. Steps finished before the error may already have made changes, and repeating them could do them twice.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model shows its checks as passed, and a new task can carry out actions.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model service. Don't turn off sign-in or certificate checks to get around this; the fix belongs on the model service.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider rejected the native tool-calling request with an error stating that automatic tool choice must be enabled (for vLLM, --enable-auto-tool-choice).

What this means

  • SMTO needs native function calls to receive an unambiguous tool name and arguments. A server can answer ordinary text while rejecting this channel. Enabling the channel also requires the parser and template to match the served model.

Why this can happen

  • SMTO needs native function calls to receive an unambiguous tool name and arguments. A server can answer ordinary text while rejecting this channel. Enabling the channel also requires the parser and template to match the served model.

How to diagnose it

  • The provider explicitly requires automatic tool calling to be enabled.
  • Recheck receives a native fixture tool call and accepts its correlated tool result.

How to fix it

  • On the provider (for vLLM), start the server with --enable-auto-tool-choice and a --tool-call-parser that matches this model and server version, and supply a compatible --chat-template if the model has none. Restart the model service, run Check saved model in Settings › Setup › Model routing, and inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.
  • Provider administrator: for vLLM, enable --enable-auto-tool-choice and select --tool-call-parser for this model and server version. Supply a compatible chat template if the model does not include one. Restart the model service with the corrected settings before submitting work again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • Recheck receives a native fixture tool call and accepts its correlated tool result.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Use the documentation for the installed vLLM release: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/tool_calling/ . No single parser works for every model. Named structured calls can remain available even if automatic tool calling is disabled.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
